description: REvil is a ransomware family that has been linked to the GOLD SOUTHFIELD group and operated as ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) since at least April 2019. REvil, which as been used against organizations in the manufacturing, transportation, and electric sectors, is highly configurable and shares code similarities with the GandCrab RaaS.

ref-cc45f09f7ef88aac1f55.text: Mosquito leverages the CreateProcess() and LoadLibrary() calls to execute files with the .dll and .exe extensions. Mosquito can launch PowerShell Scripts. Mosquito's installer uses WMI to search for antivirus display names. Mosquito’s installer is obfuscated with a custom crypter to obfuscate the installer. Mosquito executes cmd.exe and uses a pipe to read the results and send back the output to the C2 server. Mosquito can modify Registry keys under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\[dllname] to store configuration values. Mosquito also modifies Registry keys under HKCR\CLSID\...\InprocServer32 with a path to the launcher. Mosquito's installer searches the Registry and system to see if specific antivirus tools are installed on the system. Mosquito stores configuration values under the Registry key HKCU\Software\Microsoft\[dllname]. Mosquito uses a custom encryption algorithm, which consists of XOR and a stream that is similar to the Blum Blum Shub algorithm. Mosquito uses COM hijacking as a method of persistence. Mosquito deletes files using DeleteFileW API call. Mosquito's launcher uses rundll32.exe in a Registry Key value to start the main backdoor capability. Mosquito can upload and download files to the victim. Mosquito runs whoami on the victim’s machine. Mosquito uses the ipconfig command. Mosquito establishes persistence under the Registry key HKCU\Software\Run auto_update. Mosquito runs tasklist to obtain running processes.
ref-cc45f09f7ef88aac1f55.title: ESET, et al. (2018, January). Diplomats in Eastern Europe bitten by a Turla mosquito. Retrieved July 3, 2018.
